        21                  ACTING PRESIDENT CRAIG JOHNSON:

        23                  SENATOR WINNER:    -- Senator

        24       William T. "Cadillac" Smith, who ably served

        25       this Senate for 24 years, from 1962 to 1986,



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                                         2022



         1       from Big Flats, New York, and then left as the

         2       deputy majority leader.

         3                  He unfortunately passed away at the

         4       end of March, while we were away.

         5                  Senator Smith obviously served this

         6       state with great distinction and of course was

         7       known affectionately for his stunt, so to

         8       speak, in 1962, where he put a sign on the

         9       back of a Cadillac that he purchased for not

        10       growing corn as a result of the institution of

        11       the Soil Bank Program, and proceeded to use

        12       that notoriety and subsequently was elected to

        13       the New York State Senate.  He was then the

        14       president of the Farm Bureau in Big Flats,

        15       New York.

        16                  Senator Smith was well-known for a

        17       number of accomplishments while he was a

        18       member of this body.  First and foremost, he

        19       established what they called at that time the

        20       price-tag rule, which we now obviously

        21       commonly refer to as the fiscal note

        22       requirement.

        23                  At Senator Smith's insistence, that

        24       was established back when he was a young

        25       Senator, to have the first requirement that



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                                         2023



         1       all legislation that's introduced that had any

         2       fiscal implications be so indicated on the

         3       memorandums in support.

         4                  He went on to obviously also be

         5       very notorious with respect to welfare and

         6       Medicaid reform, as the chairman of the Senate

         7       Social Services Committee and also the

         8       chairman of a temporary state commission to

         9       revise the Social Services Law, which made

        10       very, very sweeping and major recommendations

        11       for reform of those two programs during the

        12       '70s.

        13                  But I think one of his lasting

        14       legacies for the State of New York was

        15       following the tragic death of his daughter,

        16       Judy, to a drunk driver in 1973, whereupon he

        17       went out and established and promoted and

        18       enacted the Stop DWI Program in 1981, which

        19       really is the cornerstone of our anti-DWI

        20       efforts in the State of New York to date.

        21                  I think he was the leading

        22       legislator in the United States at the time to

        23       establishing a very effective and far-reaching

        24       program to combat the tragedy of drunk driving

        25       in New York.  And he is probably credited,



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                                         2024



         1       along with those that supported that effort,

         2       with saving thousands of lives, not only in

         3       New York but across this country, as a result

         4       of drunk-driving fatalities that dropped some

         5       50 percent after the enactment and the

         6       enforcement of those anti-DWI efforts.  So we

         7       owe him a great deal of gratitude for those

         8       efforts.

         9                  But the Senator lived to a ripe old

        10       age of 94, and he had a great run.  And as a

        11       result, I know he loved this body and loved

        12       service here and loved his community of Big

        13       Flats, where he never forgot his roots.  So I

        14       thought that the body should be aware of the

        15       passing of a great distinguished leader of

        16       this house for many, many years.  And as such,

        17       I hope his soul rests in peace.

        18                  Thank you, Mr. President.
